Earnings Call Transcript
Six Flags (FUN) Q4 2025 Earnings Call Transcript
By

Motley Fool Transcribing

–

Updated Feb 19, 2026 at 9:12AM EST




Image source: The Motley Fool.


Date
Thursday, Feb. 19, 2026, at 8 a.m. ET
Call participants
Chief Executive Officer — John Reilly
Chief Financial Officer — Brian Witherow
Chief Strategy Officer — Michael Russell
Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email
[email protected]
Takeaways
Adjusted EBITDA
-- $165 million for the quarter on attendance of 9.3 million and revenues of $650 million.
Attendance impact
-- The elimination of winter holiday events resulted in an attendance headwind of approximately 425,000 visits; operating days totaled 779 versus 878 in the prior year.
Per capita spending
-- Per guest spending increased year over year, driven by higher admissions and in-park product purchases.
Full-year metrics
-- Net revenues reached $3.1 billion, adjusted EBITDA was $792 million, total attendance was 47.4 million, and per capita spending was $61.90.
Operating margin
-- "we closed out at 27%," with management emphasizing a mandate to improve this figure through operational initiatives.
Refinancing activity
-- Completed an oversubscribed refinancing of April 2027 notes at attractive rates, resulting in increased covenant flexibility and extended maturities.
Deferred revenue
-- Year-end deferred revenues rose approximately 1%, primarily due to higher advance sales of single-day tickets and increased group deposits.
Season pass sales
-- "sales trends of season passes and memberships have accelerated since year end," supported by the introduction of new regional pass products.
Cost synergies
-- "We have effectively delivered on 100% of those [original gross cost synergies] by the end of 2025," yet management will seek further efficiency opportunities in 2026.
CapEx guidance
-- Planned capital expenditures for 2026 are in the $400 million to $425 million range, compared to a cash spend of approximately $475 million the prior year.
Interest expense guidance
-- Interest is expected in the $135 million to $145 million range for 2026.
Operating days outlook
-- Operating days in 2026 are initially expected to be up slightly, by as much as 1% compared to 2025, with potential for increases as additional events are considered.
Asset review
-- Management confirmed ongoing disciplined asset evaluation focused on optimizing portfolio returns at individual park levels.
Regional pass uptake
-- Higher-priced regional passes are seeing greater adoption, though quantification is limited by early-cycle and partial park participation.
Cost initiatives
-- Over 300 associate-driven cost efficiency proposals have been submitted and are under active evaluation.
Priority on deleveraging
-- "all of our excess free cash flow back towards paying down debt until we get net leverage back inside of 4.0x on a sustained level."
Winter events strategy
-- Management will shift from a broad to a “returns-driven, market by market” approach in winter holiday event deployment for 2026.
Marketing spend adjustment
-- The company is shifting toward greater conversion-focused marketing and adjustments in spend timing and creative quality.
Summary
Six Flags Entertainment Corporation

(
FUN

6.20%
)
reported improved per capita guest spending and robust season pass demand, while noting lower attendance primarily due to altered holiday event strategies and reduced park operating days. Management completed the targeted synergy capture post-merger, launched a structured process for field-driven cost efficiency initiatives, and concluded an oversubscribed refinancing that extended debt maturities. The company does not plan to issue formal financial guidance at this time but indicated 2026 capital expenditures, interest expectations, and an upward trend in deferred revenue. Operational focus will intensify on localized strategies, rigorous ROI analysis for both asset and marketing investments, and sustained deleveraging using all excess free cash flow.
CEO Reilly declined to attribute 2025 performance to weakened consumer demand, stating, "We do not think this is a consumer problem. We think we can address this through improving our execution and through addressing some missteps."
Full realization of originally identified merger cost synergies was confirmed by year-end 2025, with further efficiency measures in progress for the coming year.
Winter event removals accounted for most of the attendance shortfall, but attendance and margin outlooks are guided by localized management of events and expanded operational days, especially in Mexico.
Management emphasized a shift to a more flexible, locally empowered organization and highlighted continued deployment of field-originated innovation to drive incremental margin improvement.
Industry glossary
Per capita spending
: Average total revenue generated per guest visit, including admissions and all in-park spending.
Deferred revenue
: Payments received in advance for future park visits or services, recorded as a liability until recognized as revenue upon service delivery.
Operating days
: The aggregate number of calendar days when any of the company’s parks are open for guest attendance.
Adjusted EBITDA
: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, adjusted for non-recurring or non-cash charges, used to assess operational profitability.
CapEx
: Capital expenditures, reflecting the company's investments in property, plant, equipment, and new attractions or technology.

John Reilly:
Thank you for joining us for our fourth quarter earnings call and my first earnings call as CEO of Six Flags Entertainment Corporation. On today's call, I will start by providing some background information on my experience in the industry, why I jumped at the opportunity to become Six Flags' next CEO, and my initial observations after spending the past two months on the ground. First, a little bit about me. I started out in the regional theme park business many years ago, selling popcorn as a teenager, before working my way up to executive positions in two of the world's largest regional amusement park companies, one based here in the U.S., and the other based in Europe.
Theme parks are in my blood, and I am very proud of the work I have done at each career stop to deliver exceptional experiences for our guests, to provide a fun and dynamic work environment for our team members, and to drive higher profits for our owners. So what excited me about the opportunity to join Six Flags? First, I love this industry. The regional theme park is a resilient and growing industry, with high barriers to entry leading to limited supply, resilient performance during recessions, and consistent demand when parks are well managed. In addition, Six Flags Entertainment Corporation has a dominant position within the industry, as the largest regional theme park player in the world.
Michael Russell:
Second,
John Reilly:
Six Flags parks are located in some of the largest and fastest-growing markets in North America. There are more than 200,000,000 people living within easy driving distance to our parks, providing a huge opportunity to increase our penetration and to grow attendance over time. And finally, this company has tremendous assets and significant earnings potential. Throughout my career and, particularly as I have assumed executive-level positions over the past decade, I have often been tasked with turning around underperforming assets. I can tell you this: There is no better feeling than unleashing the potential of a talented team of people to revise strategy and to improve execution, all with the goal of delivering sustained earnings growth over time.
I am not here to spend time on the past. I am here to build a disciplined operating culture that consistently delivers reliable, fun, and memorable guest experiences, as well as dependable financial outcomes, and to earn credibility with our guests and investors quarter by quarter. This role is personal for me. Growing up in the theme park industry, I know what great looks like. Over the past several weeks, I have been spending time in our parks. A lot of time. Walking the midways, meeting with park leadership teams, conducting focus groups with guests, and engaging with our frontline associates. Those visits have been invaluable, and they have reinforced my conviction about the underlying strength of our company.
What I have seen reinforces two things: The underlying demand is there, and the biggest value creation opportunity is through better execution. Let me just share a few examples from my park visits, because I believe they highlight the kind of high-return work that can change consumer perception and quickly improve results. At Six Flags Magic Mountain, I visited the park's maintenance shops during my tour, and from my interactions there, it was clear the maintenance team took great pride in their efforts this past year to restore coaster trains, put them back into service, driving better ride uptime, more rides for guests, and higher guest satisfaction.
With a fleet of more than 60 coaster trains, we will benefit from their hard work and our investments even more so going forward. We are already seeing positive signs of this work and investment in guest KPIs in 2025 and early in the 2026 season. We expect to see significantly increased ride uptime and throughput at Magic Mountain and at other parks. Important work like this is going on in all operating areas across our parks. On the food and beverage front, we have placed executive chefs in the park to elevate food quality and improve guest satisfaction.
During my tour of Carowinds, Eraj, our executive chef there, showed me how innovations are expanding the park's menu offering this year, and he and his team explained how they are more efficiently approaching food preparation during varying demand levels, with monitored holding times to ensure guests are getting the freshest and best-quality food. The placement of chefs has been fully deployed already, and now with the right resources in place, we are positioned to reliably deliver higher quality food across our parks. Our scale provides us with a clear mandate to constantly improve efficiency.
As I have traveled to parks and conducted leadership town halls, I am encouraged that our park teams are not only embracing the challenge, but taking pride in driving efficiency. They are committed to do this work the right way, always protecting the guest experience. When I visited Kings Island, our maintenance team shared their idea how we could save thousands by purchasing certain equipment we are currently renting. I can assure you this is something we are digging into further.
During my stop at Canada's Wonderland, Vivendra, our workforce director, proudly explained how his efforts ensured labor is being scheduled according to forecasted demand levels, so that park labor is deployed at the right time and the right place throughout our entire enterprise. Effectiveness in this area helps reduce costs and ultimately helps drive improved guest spending. The workforce management program was deployed across the portfolio year, and now we stand to benefit from the resources and systems that are in place to drive efficiency and increase reliability in our business. Having been through this process a number of times, I can assure you this: The best ideas and highest-return innovations come from the people closest to the work.
At Six Flags, that is our ride operators, our maintenance teams, food and retail leaders, call center teams, finance and accounting staff, among others.
